title: Tab switching reportedly loses the scroll offset - key identity ruled out, save/restore path unexamined
outcome:
PRINCIPAL REPORT (2026-09-09, verbatim): "przelaczenie pomiedzy tabami, nie trzyma
offsetu" - switching between tabs does not hold the scroll offset.

STATUS: UNREPRODUCED. No failing test exists. Parked at the principal's
instruction after the key-identity space was exhausted. Everything below is
reading of code and of live state, not observed behaviour.

WHY THIS ENTRY IS MOSTLY NEGATIVE RESULTS: three separate mechanisms were
proposed and refuted within an hour. Recording only the surviving question
would guarantee that the next reader re-walks all three. The refutations are
the expensive part; keep them.

RULED OUT 1 - "the fix is not deployed."
  6759c84 ("Put a returning reader back on the message they were reading",
  exact offset) IS AN ANCESTOR of the deployed commit 4dec5eb
  (git merge-base --is-ancestor exit 0). The served bundle
  assets/index-Bbb5ixK0.js (1,234,800 bytes, sha256
  F50C758E1687C51671929AD06CC31CFD18A063EE6A395AA34426E150C1B3A559) contains
  all nine scroll-key literals and position_restore. 0e7ab55 touched the
  scroll area in ONE file only, App.scroll-behavior.test.tsx, +17 lines - a
  test, zero product lines. CONSEQUENCE: a rebuild and redeploy would not
  change a single line of scroll product code. Green obtained from such a
  rebuild would look like a result and be none.

RULED OUT 2 - "six tab kinds share one scroll key because the resolver has no
case for them."
  resolveSessionPaneScrollStateKey has cases for 9 of the 15 WorkspaceTab
  kinds; session, responseBoard, controlPanel, orchestratorList, sessionList
  and projectList fall to the default branch. The default returns
  `${paneId}:${viewMode}:${activeSessionId}` and PaneViewMode CONTAINS EXACTLY
  THOSE NAMES, so those kinds are discriminated by viewMode rather than by a
  case label. The nine explicit cases exist for kinds that can appear in a
  pane in MULTIPLE INSTANCES (two source tabs, two terminals, two canvases),
  where viewMode alone cannot separate them.
  METHOD DEFECT WORTH KEEPING: this hypothesis was built on six ABSENT string
  literals in the served bundle. PRESENCE OF A LITERAL PROVES PRESENCE;
  ABSENCE DOES NOT PROVE ABSENCE - the default branch constructs those
  segments dynamically from viewMode, so zero occurrences of ":session:" is
  fully consistent with the segment being produced at runtime.

RULED OUT 3 - "two session tabs in one pane collide because activeSession
falls back to sessionTabs[0]."
  SessionPaneView.active-context.ts resolves activeSession from
  pane.activeSessionId, then sessionTabs[0]?.session, then null. But
  workspace.ts:2219 sets `activeSessionId: activeTab.sessionId` when a session
  tab is activated, so the field FOLLOWS THE TAB and two session tabs yield
  different keys. workspace.ts:461-464 additionally NULLS a stale
  activeSessionId during reconciliation instead of leaving it stale.
  LIVE CONFIRMATION (read-only GET /api/state and /api/workspaces/<id> against
  the running instance; nothing mutated, SQLite not opened): 8 workspaces, 21
  panes, 1448 sessions, and ZERO unresolvable activeSessionId. The
  precondition for the fallback was not present in the reporter's own state.
  A narrow window survives - after reconciliation nulls the field and BEFORE
  the first tab activation - but activation itself closes it, so it does not
  produce "switching does not hold the offset."

ESTABLISHED AND USEFUL:
  - The reported scenario EXISTS in the live layout: six panes hold 2-3
    session tabs with distinct session ids (Termal 2, Engram 3 and 2,
    Phoenix 2, CV 3, Legal 3), all at viewMode=session. With two session tabs
    in one pane the only key discriminator is the session id.
  - Scroll positions live IN MEMORY: App.tsx:561 paneScrollPositionsRef,
    shape Record<paneId, Record<key, {anchor?, shouldStick, top}>>. They are
    NOT in the server layout (pane objects carry no scroll fields, confirmed
    against the live layout documents) and not in browser storage. The ref
    survives a tab switch because App does not unmount, so PERSISTENCE
    LIFETIME IS EXCLUDED as a cause.
  - Deployed code equals tree for the relevant files: git diff between 4dec5eb
    and the worktree is EMPTY for both ui/src/workspace.ts and
    ui/src/SessionPaneView.scroll-key.ts. The conclusions above therefore
    describe the running code, not merely the repository.

REMAINING SPACE - EXACTLY TWO POSSIBILITIES:
  1. The departing tab's offset is not written before the content remounts.
  2. It is written, and the restore does not apply it.

LEAD (UNVERIFIED): activating a session tab changes activeSessionId AND
viewMode together (workspace.ts:2219-2221). The position key contains both, so
a tab switch moves the key on two fields at once. If the save targets the old
key after pane state has already advanced to the new viewMode, that is
shape 1. Not measured.

EXISTING COVERAGE THAT DOES NOT REPRODUCE IT: App.scroll-behavior.test.tsx
"restores an attached virtualized session before the first frame after a tab
switch" passes. It switches to an attached virtualized session - a case the
default branch handles correctly. NO TEST COVERS A SWITCH BETWEEN TWO SESSION
TABS IN ONE PANE.

NEXT STEP WHEN RESUMED: write that red test FIRST. A test that is green on
arrival proves nothing here, because every mechanism examined so far is green
and the symptom was still reported.

FASTEST DISAMBIGUATION, COSTS THE PRINCIPAL ONE SENTENCE: were both tabs
SESSIONS in the SAME pane, and did it happen right after startup or during
normal work? If either tab was a control panel or a list, hypothesis space 3
and its remnants close entirely.

RELATED: tm-8p62 records the missing-signal defect that made the original
report expensive to diagnose. That entry stands; its incident narrative is
now superseded on one point - the fix has since been deployed.
